name: USSF-432
destination_explanation: It starts around 160 km up and runs to about 2,000 km. At this height a satellite goes all the way around the planet in about an hour and a half.
slot_a_text: A classified mission for the United States Space Force. It is possibly a batch of classified LEO satellites based on SpaceX’s Starshield satellite bus, based on locations of rocket stage drop zones being exact fits with previous Starlink Group 15 launches.
slot_b_text: B1095 is out on its 8th flight. It came down on the drone ship Of Course I Still Love You, 574 km downrange. Its previous trip was GPS III SV10, about 7 months ago.

lg_slot_a_text: A classified mission for the United States Space Force. It is possibly a batch of classified LEO satellites based on SpaceX’s Starshield satellite bus, based on locations of rocket stage drop zones being exact fits with previous Starlink Group 15 launches.
lg_slot_b_text: That was B1095's 8th flight in 18 months. Mostly Starlink: six of them, one GPS, and one USSF. At its fastest it was back on the pad in 37 days. It has flown from three different pads.
lg_slot_c_text: That was SpaceX's 125th launch of the year, 744th all time. That is a launch every other day. Falcon 9 has not lost a mission in 347 flights.
